A Diplomats' Dinner marked the conclusion of the conference, bringing together guests, delegates and organizers.
BUFTIMUN 2026 provided students with a platform to develop leadership, critical thinking, negotiation and communication skills while promoting diplomatic awareness, international understanding and constructive dialogue.
Through its fourth edition, BUFTMUN reaffirmed its commitment to nurturing future leaders and encouraging youth engagement in global affairs.

item.title: Police killings, station arson fuel public anxiety
item.description:
Police officers are being killed while trying to arrest criminals. Handcuffed suspects are being snatched from police custody, patrol teams are coming under attack, government firearms are being looted and police stations are being set ablaze.
At a time when the police are entrusted with protecting people's lives and property, the security of the force's own members has emerged as a major concern.
From isolated criminal incidents to political violence, repeated attacks on police are not only putting officers at greater risk but also testing the state's law enforcement capacity and authority.
More than nine months have passed since the government led by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman took office on February 17. During this period, 400 attacks on police were recorded across the country between March and October. The number rose to 484 between January and October.
Attacks continued in different parts of the country in November, leaving one police member dead. Two police stations in Gopalganj were also attacked, torched and looted, while police vehicles and installations came under attack elsewhere.
According to monthly crime statistics from the Police Headquarters and data from the Bangladesh Police Association, police faced 484 attacks across the country between January and October this year. Four police members were killed and 370 seriously injured in these incidents.
With the killing of a police member in Narayanganj on November 22, the death toll from attacks on police this year has risen to at least five. In the first 23 days of November, at least 21 police members were injured in multiple attacks.
An analysis of the figures shows that April recorded the highest number of attacks, with 66 incidents, followed by 63 in March and 55 in May.
Although attacks declined somewhat from June, the monthly figure never fell below 40. The number rose again in October and November.
Recent incidents, however, point to an increasingly alarming pattern, with police members being killed, stations torched, firearms looted and arrested suspects forcibly freed by organised groups.
In the latest incident, Constable Anwar Molla was killed when miscreants attacked him while he was gathering intelligence in plain clothes in Fatullah, Narayanganj, on Sunday.
ASI Abdus Sattar, who was accompanying him, survived the attack. He was later placed on closed duty and attached to the police lines.
Earlier, Police Inspector Md Shah Alam was killed in an attack by miscreants on October 8 while returning from an operation in Rupsha, Khulna.
In the first week of September, Special Branch Sub-Inspector Altaf Hossain was beaten to death in Aminbazar, Savar. He was attacked after protesting the assault of a man.
At least 11 attacks targeting members of the police and Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) have reportedly taken place in Narayanganj alone since March this year.
Law enforcement personnel have come under attack while conducting operations and for taking action against drug traders.
On November 5, Armed Police Battalion (APBn) member Abul Kalam was allegedly brutally tortured by drug traders in Rupganj, Narayanganj, for opposing their activities.
On November 10, three members of the district Detective Branch (DB) police were attacked while conducting an anti-drug drive at Kushtia Government College.
Alongside attacks on individual officers, police stations have increasingly become targets of violence. Within just a few days, two police stations in Gopalganj came under attack, with incidents of vandalism, arson and looting reported.
On November 17, Tungipara Police Station was attacked and set on fire, and firearms were looted. According to the Bangladesh Police Association, the attack damaged the station's infrastructure and a large number of vehicles. Government-owned firearms, along with weapons deposited by members of the public, were also looted.
Two days later, on November 19, Muksudpur Police Station came under attack and was set ablaze. Important documents, police vehicles and seized vehicles were destroyed in the fire.
Leaders and activists of the activities-banned Awami League and its student wing, Bangladesh Chhatra League, have been accused of carrying out the attacks.
The arson attacks have disrupted routine operations at both police stations, leaving local residents facing difficulties in accessing police services.
A police box in Muradpur, Chittagong, was also set on fire on November 18.
The damage caused by an attack on a police station extends far beyond its building, furniture and vehicles. The destruction of case records, crime-related information and preserved evidence can seriously hamper investigations and judicial proceedings in the long run.
Such attacks can also undermine public safety and restrict residents' access to essential law enforcement services.
The growing number of incidents in which suspects are forcibly freed from police custody has emerged as another major concern for the force.
After arrests, organised groups are launching attacks on police to free suspects before they can be produced before a court.
On November 22, an attack on Akhaura Police Station in Brahmanbaria and a clash with police erupted over the arrest of Sayeb Ali, an accused in an explosives case and joint convener of the upazila unit of the National Citizen Party (NCP).
At least seven police members were injured in the incident.
Earlier, on November 6, a suspect in a fraud case was snatched from police custody in Sonatala, Bogra. The attackers also vandalised a police vehicle.
Similar incidents occurred in Shantiganj, Sunamganj, in September and Kutubdia, Cox's Bazar, in July, where attackers assaulted police and snatched arrested suspects.
These incidents are creating fresh challenges for law enforcement agencies. Police now have to make additional security arrangements even for routine tasks such as executing arrest warrants and conducting regular operations.
Those concerned say the attacks on police have different underlying causes. In some cases, organised criminal groups are resisting law enforcement operations. In others, attempts to exert political influence and a growing tendency to take the law into one's own hands through mob violence are contributing to the violence.
Another major concern is the lack of clarity over the progress of investigations and trials in cases involving attacks on police.
Although reports of cases being filed and suspects arrested emerge after such incidents, no information was available on how many investigations had been completed or how many charge sheets had been submitted.
The impact of the police's use of lethal force during the 2024 mass uprising, as well as the subsequent violence against the force, continues to linger.
Even as the police struggle to overcome the crisis of professionalism, morale and public trust stemming from that period, their members are once again facing a sustained wave of attacks.
Dr Touhidul Haque, an associate professor at the Institute of Social Welfare and Research at Dhaka University and a crime analyst, told Dhaka Tribune that recurring attacks on police in different parts of the country were a matter of serious concern for law and order.
"This is not merely a matter of the security of police personnel; it is also linked to the state's capacity and authority to enforce the law. When criminals attack police in organised groups or snatch suspects from custody, a sense of insecurity spreads among ordinary people as well. A culture of impunity, political influence, a lack of public trust in police and the increasingly reckless behaviour of criminals may be contributing to these incidents," he said.
He said those involved must face swift investigations and visible justice, irrespective of their political affiliations.
"At the same time, rebuilding police professionalism, accountability and public trust is essential. Otherwise, such incidents could further complicate the law and order situation," he added.
Police Headquarters officials say officers often come under attack while trying to control unruly situations. They also believe that certain groups are still attempting to create instability in public life.
However, they said police were continuing to perform their duties to address the situation. Cases were being filed over attacks and violence, and those accused were being brought before the courts.
Kamarum Munira, assistant inspector general (Media and Public Relations) at the Police Headquarters, told Dhaka Tribune that investigations were underway to determine whether the attacks were part of any deliberate plan.
"Attacks aimed at undermining the morale of law enforcement personnel or obstructing police from performing their duties will not be tolerated," she said.
She said instructions had been issued to strengthen the security of frontline police personnel, maintain heightened vigilance in vulnerable areas, increase intelligence surveillance and identify those involved in the attacks to bring them to justice.
She added that the authorities were also placing emphasis on providing police members with necessary security equipment and training.
"Police work to protect people's lives and property. An attack on police is therefore an attack on the state's responsibility to maintain law and order. The police will take strict legal action to prevent such crimes," she said.

item.title: Misuse, weaknesses of child marriage law upheld at media dialogue
item.description:
Debate for Democracy Chairman Hasan Ahamed Chowdhury Kiron on Tuesday said a special provision of the Child Marriage Restraint Act 2017 is being misused, giving child marriage legal cover and deepening poverty and inequality among girls.
“Taking advantage of the weakness of this provision, child marriage is gaining legal footing, and the number of such marriages is rising,” he said, according to a press release.
He made these remarks while speaking at a media dialogue titled “Child Marriage Law Reform” at a hotel in the capital, organised by UNFPA Bangladesh.
Kiron said Section 19 of the law is meant to be an exception. According to him, it provides that if a 16-year-old girl is married for ‘justifiable reasons’ with the consent of her parents or a court, the marriage will not be treated as child marriage.
He alleged that child marriage figures were also concealed during the previous government's tenure.
He claimed the data provided by the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS) was incorrect, citing the 2022 census, which put the country's population at 16.98 crore.
"People laughed at that figure," Kiron said, adding that the country still cannot say its actual population or child marriage rate.
Jamuna Television Head of News Towhidul Islam said the provision should be amended as it is discriminatory.
He also demanded scrapping the provision that holds minors responsible for child marriage.
Towhidul pointed to what he described as a 300% difference in child marriage rates between Rajshahi and Sylhet divisions, calling the gap questionable.
He said efforts should be made to apply the experience of Sylhet, which he said is ahead, in Rajshahi and Khulna.
Speakers said nearly half of the girls in Bangladesh are still victims of child marriage, which leads to adolescent pregnancy and limits their opportunities in life.
They stressed that the media has a vital role in bringing about change.
UNFPA Bangladesh Representative Catherine Breen Kamkong attended as the chief guest.
Dhaka Tribune Editor Reaz Ahmad and RTV Head of News Elias Hossain, among others, also spoke.

item.title: Awami League leader shot dead in Khulna
item.description:
A leader of the activities-banned Awami League was shot dead in Khulna on Tuesday night.
The deceased, Abdul Halim Sheikh, 45, was shot in the Kalpataru Market area under Daulatpur Police Station around 8pm.
He was rushed to Khulna Medical College Hospital in a bloodied condition, where doctors declared him dead upon arrival.
Halim was a former organising secretary of the Awami League's Ward No 4 unit under Khulna City Corporation (KCC).
He was also reportedly involved in the politics of the Ward No 4 unit of Jubo League.
Daulatpur Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Muradul Islam said the shooting took place in the Kalpataru Market area, leaving Halim critically wounded.
He said the identities of the attackers and the motive behind the killing were not immediately known. Police are investigating the incident.
Halim sustained gunshot wounds to his head and chest.

item.title: Five killed in bus-auto-rickshaw collision in Cox’s Bazar
item.description:
Five passengers of a CNG-run auto-rickshaw were killed in a head-on collision with a bus in Eidgaon upazila of Cox’s Bazar on Tuesday evening.
The accident occurred around 6:30pm in the Fakirabazar area on the Chittagong-Cox’s Bazar Highway, said Eidgaon Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) ATM Sifatul Majdar.
Police said three passengers died on the spot, while the other two succumbed to their injuries on the way to Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital. The victims included four men and a woman.
Three of the deceased were identified as Sahab Uddin and Jasim Uddin of Nalbania in Khutakhali union of Chakaria upazila, and Saiful Islam of Lama upazila in Bandarban. The identities of the other two victims, including the woman, could not be immediately known.
According to police and local sources, the Hanif Paribahan bus was travelling from Chittagong to Cox’s Bazar, while the auto-rickshaw was heading towards Chakaria from Cox’s Bazar.
The vehicles collided head-on in front of Eidgaon Police Station, leaving the auto-rickshaw badly mangled and all five passengers dead.
The accident brought traffic on the highway to a halt, leaving hundreds of vehicles stranded on both sides. Vehicles travelling between Dhaka, Chittagong and Cox’s Bazar were among those caught in the congestion.
Traffic movement resumed around 8pm after police brought the situation under control.
OC ATM Sifatul Majdar said the bodies were being sent to the Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital morgue for autopsies. He added that traffic on the highway returned to normal after 8pm.

item.title: Ex-MP Azizul Islam sent to jail in Explosive Substances Act case
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Tuesday sent former Jessore-6 independent MP Mohammad Azizul Islam to jail after rejecting his bail petition in an Explosive Substances Act case filed with Mohammadpur Police Station.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Hasibuzzaman passed the order on Tuesday following an application by the investigation officer, Sub-Inspector Md Khair Uddin Bhuiyan of the Detective Branch's (DB) Tejgaon zone.
SI Md Mizanur Rahman of the prosecution department confirmed the matter.
Azizul Islam's lawyer, Md Kayes Ahmed Arnab, sought bail on his behalf.
The hearing was held in the judge's chamber without producing the accused before the court. After hearing both sides, the court rejected the bail petition and ordered that he be sent to jail.
According to the investigation officer's application, several accused named in the case, along with unidentified individuals, gathered near Beribadh Tin Rasta in Mohammadpur around 7:55pm on November 18 with plans to carry out subversive activities.
Acting on a tip-off, a DB team from the Tejgaon division raided the area around 8:50pm. Several named suspects were detained, while the others fled.
During the operation, police seized around 140 grams of a yellow, sulphur-like substance wrapped in a blue polythene packet from one of the detained suspects. Preliminary interrogation suggested that the substance had been kept for making crude bombs, the application said.
Police later filed a case under the Explosive Substances Act with Mohammadpur Police Station over the incident.
Based on information obtained during the investigation, a DB team from the Tejgaon zone arrested Azizul Islam from Lalmatia in Mohammadpur around 4:20pm on November 23.
Azizul Islam is the son of the late Khandaker Rafiquzzaman of Brahmakati area under Keshabpur Municipality in Jessore. He had been living in a residence in Block A/P of Lalmatia.
He is also a former joint convener of the Keshabpur upazila unit of Bangladesh Chhatra League.

item.title: Journalist mugged again five days after filing police case
item.description:
A journalist of the daily Kaler Kantho was robbed and assaulted again on Tuesday night, just five days after he reported an earlier mugging to police.
Gaus Rahman Piyas, news editor of the newspaper's multimedia department, was attacked in front of Dhanmondi Boys' High School, opposite Road 27 in Dhanmondi, around 10:30pm.
Piyas said he was first mugged at around 11am on November 17 in front of the Airport Toll Plaza on the Dhaka Elevated Expressway.
He filed a general diary (GD) with Airport Police Station the same day and subsequently filed a case there on the afternoon of November 23.
He alleged that he received no additional security despite filing the case. On Tuesday night, while returning home from work, he was attacked by muggers in front of Dhanmondi Boys' High School.
The attackers assaulted him, leaving him injured, and snatched his mobile phone and wallet. They also threatened to kill him at knifepoint.
Recalling the first incident, Piyas said one of the muggers had got out of a vehicle, snatched his mobile phone and fled.
Following the two consecutive attacks, the journalist expressed concern over his safety and frustration over the police response.
Airport Police Station Officer-in-Charge Kamrul Islam Talukder said the case was being treated seriously and efforts were underway to arrest those involved.
Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station OC Muhammad Shahidul Islam also said police were working to apprehend the muggers.

item.title: De Bruyne still 'loves' City owners despite financial charges
item.description:
Kevin De Bruyne said on Monday his love for Manchester City's leadership has not been tainted by a guilty verdict on breaking financial rules, that could tarnish his legacy at the English giants.
Napoli playmaker De Bruyne returns to the Etihad Stadium in Champions League action on Tuesday, just over a year since his decade in Manchester came to an end.
De Bruyne won six Premier League titles and the Champions League during a golden era for City to become one of the club's all-time greats.
However, some of those titles could be stripped unless City successfully overturn a ruling that found them guilty on more than 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules between 2009 and 2018.
"I'm proud of what I've done as a football player, and honestly, this is my club. I love the owners," De Bruyne told reporters.
"I've even spoken to (chairman) Khaldoon (Al Mubarak) about how to buy a club.
"I have nothing but affection for this club and that will never change, (the way) the people treated me and my family for 10 years."
The Belgian also dismissed suggestions his achievements on the field are now tainted in light of City's financial impropriety.
"In life there are rules, but everybody plays on the limit," he said.
"I played in between the white lines. I competed with other players and I had many experiences with my teams, with the players. That's the thing that I value most."
Napoli are in danger of an early Champions League exit after losing three of their opening four European games of the season.
The Italians sit 27th in the 36-team table with only the top 24 progressing.
City's form in the Premier League has slumped since their future in the English top-flight was plunged into doubt by the guilty verdict.
A severe points deduction and possibly even relegation from the Premier League is expected if City's appeal is not upheld.
But Enzo Maresca's men have won three of their four Champions League games to occupy a place in the top eight, who progress directly to the last 16.

item.title: Brentford hit Everton for four to soar into Premier League top six
item.description:
Keane Lewis-Potter struck twice as Brentford battered 10-man Everton 4-0 to climb into the Premier League's top six on Monday.
Lewis-Potter's luck was in as twice he saw deflected efforts leave Jordan Pickford stranded before a wild challenge by captain James Tarkowski left Everton a man down for over half the match.
Vitaly Janelt's stunning strike from long range and Fabio Carvalho rounded off a comfortable victory for the Bees, who will fancy their chances when they travel to struggling Manchester United on Saturday.
"It'll probably go a bit under the radar because of the sending off but 11 versus 11 we were outstanding," said Brentford boss Keith Andrews.
"I'm really happy with the group, the club and long may it continue.
"Long way to go. Onto Old Trafford on Saturday and we're really looking forward to it."
David Moyes's record 593rd game as Everton boss was not one the Scot will want to remember as his side were swatted aside in west London despite having the chance to go fifth in the table.
"With two shots, both deflected in and took the goalkeeper the wrong way, and the third goal was a worldie outside the box. We could use them as excuses but there's no excuses tonight," said Moyes.
"The performance was way below the standards we've set and the way we've been playing recently."
A defensive mix-up allowed Jaidon Anthony too much time to pick out Lewis-Potter for the opening goal and his shot deflected off Jarrad Branthwaite to wrong-foot Pickford.
Two minutes later, Everton failed to deal with a free-kick into the box and Lewis-Potter was given two opportunities to double his tally.
The winger's first effort was blocked by Tarkowski before Thierno Barry this time deflected into his own net as the Frenchman threw himself towards the ball.
Worse was to come for the visitors when their skipper was shown red after a VAR review for catching Yehor Yarmoliuk on the shin.
Tarkowski will now be banned for Sunday's Merseyside derby at home to Liverpool.
Moyes turned to Jack Grealish off the bench at half-time in his first appearance since being dropped for breaching club discipline a month ago.
Grealish could do little to inspire the 10 men as Janelt's strike lit up an otherwise uneventful second half.
The German midfielder blasted into the top corner from well outside the box 23 minutes from time.
Carvalho rounded off the scoring from point-blank range when a corner fell to the former Liverpool winger in the 90th minute.
Brentford will head to Old Trafford for Mauricio Pochettino's first home match in charge of United full of confidence and eager to inflict more woe on the Red Devils.
United sit second bottom of the table after a nine-game winless league run, plunging the English giants into danger of being relegated for the first time in 52 years.

item.title: 'Issues and disputes' put India's Olympic bid under scrutiny
item.description:
India must urgently resolve internal disputes dogging its Olympic association to strengthen its chances of hosting the 2036 Games, experts warn, as the country's bid comes under scrutiny on Thursday.
The International Olympic Committee this month expressed disappointment over "extremely regrettable" schisms within the IOA, warning they were damaging the reputation of the Olympic movement in India.
India is among seven countries interested in hosting the 2036 Olympics alongside Germany, Hungary, Qatar, South Africa, South Korea and Turkey.
The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) and other stakeholders will present their case to the IOC's Future Host Commission in Switzerland on Thursday.
India's delegation is expected to include IOA president P.T. Usha, IOC member Nita Ambani and government representatives including officials from Gujarat, the state where proposed host city Ahmedabad is located and the home state of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
"There is a massive governance flaw that has not been addressed," sports writer Sharda Ugra told AFP.
"I think setting the house in order has to start -- they don't even accept that the house is a problem."
- 'Not going away' -
IOA executive council elections are scheduled for December 5 but controversy erupted after Usha was initially excluded from the contest for a second term as president, amid allegations of fraud in the nomination process.
The former sprinter, who became the first woman to lead the IOA in 2022, later entered the presidential race after being nominated by another national federation.
Usha, 62, a member of parliament's upper house, alleged that a "big fraud" had been carried out.
"Winning and losing is normal but results have to be fair," she told The Tribune newspaper.
Ugra said the problems could not be concealed by a polished presentation.
"No matter what you show in your PowerPoint presentation and in your video (to the IOC), this is not going away," she said.
The IOA faced major governance and constitutional disputes in 2022 over a failure to comply with India's sports development code.
Judicial intervention was needed to overhaul its constitution and electoral framework, but similar problems have resurfaced ahead of next month's elections.
The sports ministry declined to comment.
The IOA did not publicly respond to the IOC warning.
- 'Extremely regrettable' -
The IOC, in its letter to the IOA earlier this month, said it was "very disappointed to note that, once again, issues and disputes seem to have resurfaced in the conduct of the IOA election process and in the implementation of the rules governing the IOA elections".
"This extremely regrettable situation is, once again, negatively affecting the operations and reputation of the Olympic Movement in India," the IOC said.
Veteran sports journalist G. Rajaraman said the IOC's displeasure should not cause panic.
"I don't think it will have a deep impact on the whole process of host city nomination," Rajaraman told AFP.
"I think the process will go through smoothly," he added, pointing out that the presentation will be led by the Gujarat state authorities.
Rajaraman said a lack of administrative experience among some former athletes remained a challenge for sports governance, which required specialist expertise.
"I think athletes should come up step-by-step in administration, and not parachuted into the top positions."
Ahmedabad will host the 2030 Commonwealth Games, seen as a major rehearsal for an Olympics.
The city is also home to the world's largest cricket stadium.
The 2028 Olympics will take place in Los Angeles and Brisbane will host in 2032.

item.title: Cricket's saliva ban to stay despite Gill call to overturn rule
item.description:
The International Cricket Council has no plans to reverse the ban on applying saliva to shine the ball, despite India skipper Shubman Gill's call to allow the practice again.
Gill on Monday said the ban should be revoked to help bowlers get reverse swing, after India's high-scoring opening Test in Wellington against New Zealand ended in a draw.
However, AFP understands that the ICC has no immediate plans to relax the rule, which is treated in the same way as any other unfair method of changing the ball's condition.
Saliva can materially alter the ball when mixed with sweets, chewing gum and mints and the practice is incredibly hard to monitor and regulate.
The ICC temporarily barred the practice of applying saliva as a precautionary measure during the pandemic in 2020 and two years later made it permanent.
The use of saliva to shine one side of the old ball and keep the other rough helps fast bowlers get the leather ball to swing late.
"I don't understand why we haven't been allowed to shine the ball yet -- we are way past Covid times," Gill said after the draw.
"There was a rule that you can't put saliva on the ball to make it shine. It's been seven-eight years and I still don't understand why they are not allowing it.
"I think this is also a big factor (in bowlers struggling to get wickets)."
The tourists had declared their first innings on a mammoth 720-9 midway through the fourth day, but New Zealand survived 120 overs to finish on 239-5 at the close.
The Indian Premier League lifted its saliva ban last year, much to the bowlers' delight, but the ICC finds no reason to relax it in international matches.
India and New Zealand now head to Christchurch for the second and deciding Test starting Friday, where both captains expect a more typical green, grassy and seamer-friendly wicket.

item.title: Bayern score 'own goal' as Musiala firestorm builds
item.description:
Already ravaged by injuries, Bayern Munich head to Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday swept up in a firestorm of their own making over star midfielder Jamal Musiala.
Currently 13th in the table, Bayern need points if they are to reach the top eight and avoid a punishing extra knockout round.
While Lille are languishing in 35th spot and last season's semi-finalists Bayern limp into the clash despite being one of the leading contenders.
Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane was the latest to join Bayern's bulging casualty ward with an ankle injury on Friday which will likely rule him out until February.
But while Musiala returned after a two-month absence in last week's match, club bosses were accused of launching a coordinated effort to pressure the midfielder into accepting a pay cut.
That the club decided to kick-start the furore a day before announcing record revenues of close to a billion euros has not gone unnoticed.
- 'Own goal' -
In August, Musiala revealed he was suffering from a "neurological disorder" which can lead to "temporary but treatable seizures", having collapsed twice on the field in pre-season.
After his return, club powerbroker Karl-Heinz Rummenigge told German TV the 23-year-old midfielder was unlikely to recapture his previous form due to the condition -- and should consider taking a pay cut.
"If he doesn't return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency -- because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable," Rummenigge told Sky Germany.
Rummenigge's statements were striking but echoed those made by former president and fellow powerbroker Uli Hoeness, along with current CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen.
On Sunday, player union FIFPRO slammed Bayern, accusing the club of a "coordinated campaign to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives" to accept a wage cut.
"A club of Bayern's standing should know better," FIFPRO said in a statement.
FIFPRO's German counterparts VDV joined the chorus on Monday, saying the comments would "leave a lasting impression" on Musiala and on the club in general.
"I believe those in charge have scored a real 'own goal' here," VDV president Carsten Ramelow said in a statement.
World Cup and Ballon d'Or winner Lothar Matthaeus, who has never been afraid to butt heads with Hoeness and the Bayern brass, said the club should provide Musiala with "every bit of support."
"Right now, everything is being placed on Musiala's shoulders," Matthaeus told RTL.
"Perhaps all parties can sit down and talk later at a more opportune moment," he added.
- An opportunity for Musiala -
For their part, Bayern coach Vincent Kompany and powerful sporting director Max Eberl have thrown their support behind Musiala publicly.
Kompany, who himself returned on Friday from a month out after being hospitalised with meningeal irritation in October, backed Musiala.
"The coach must be the one to believe in the player. And if we manage to bring him back, then everyone wins: the club, the fans -- and all of German football."
Eberl said on Friday he was confident Musiala would return to his best form if given the chance.
Bayern's injury crisis has provided Musiala with an opportunity to illustrate his importance to the club by starring in the coming months.
Besides Kane, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and captain Manuel Neuer will miss Wednesday's match.
Michael Olise and Luis Diaz are also injury doubts, meaning the only recognised fit forward is 18-year-old winger Lennart Karl.
Musiala has not addressed the controversy directly, but gave an insight into how he shuts out pressure and critique at a fan event this weekend.
Asked by a fan how he handled the weight of expectation, Musiala said he was still in the process of finding the right approach.
"I'm still learning... Too much pressure isn't good, but a hunger for victory is important," Musiala said.
"Finding that balance is a very important part of life."

item.title: What happens if a nuclear weapon explodes in space?
item.description:
A nuclear explosion in space would be unlikely to cause widespread injuries on Earth. But it could disable satellites that provide services we depend on every day, including some that save lives.
In the United States, satellite failures could make it harder for emergency crews to communicate in remote areas. If GPS were also disrupted, drivers and pilots could lose navigation guidance, and financial networks could lose a source of precise time.
We have some idea of what would happen because it’s already been done.
On the evening of July 8, 1962, people in Hawaii held “watch-the-bomb parties” and followed the countdown on shortwave radio. Then the night sky lit up. The United States had detonated a nuclear weapon about 400 kilometers above the Pacific. The test was called Starfish Prime.
An electromagnetic pulse knocked out some streetlights in Hawaii, and some Pacific radio links briefly went down. The glow faded within minutes, but some satellites failed months later.
The air was too thin for a conventional fireball to form or for a destructive shock wave to reach the ground. Charged particles made denser air below glow, creating an artificial aurora. The atmosphere also absorbed much of the initial radiation.
Satellites are especially vulnerable because they orbit above most of the atmosphere that shields people on the ground from the initial radiation.
In orbit, the initial burst of X-rays can damage spacecraft right away. But Earth’s magnetic field can also trap electrons released after the blast, as it did after Starfish Prime. Satellites receive another dose each time they cross the resulting radiation belt. Over time, that exposure can damage electronics and solar panels.
That would depend on where the explosion happened and which satellites crossed the radiation belt. GPS satellites send signals that help phones, planes and ships work out where they are. They orbit about 20,200 kilometers above Earth and could keep working even if satellites closer to Earth failed.
But satellites do different jobs. A ship’s emergency beacon can use GPS to work out its location, then send it to rescuers through a separate satellite network. If part of that network failed, the alert could take longer to get through.
The 1967 Outer Space Treaty bars its parties from placing nuclear weapons in orbit. The 1963 Limited Test Ban Treaty prohibits its parties from carrying out nuclear explosions in space.
The Outer Space Treaty has no dedicated system for checking what spacecraft carry. A detonation is easier to detect because US satellite sensors are designed to pick up the signals it gives off.
Shielding could help protect satellite electronics, and backups could keep some services running. During a GPS outage, pilots over the contiguous US can use ground-based navigation aids. Operators could launch replacements, but those satellites could still face lingering radiation or debris.
Radiation could leave many satellites intact but unable to steer. If two objects collided, fragments from the crash could hit other satellites, creating more debris and triggering further collisions. If enough debris built up for the chain reaction to keep going on its own, it could continue even if no new satellites were launched. This is known as Kessler syndrome.
Whether an explosion would trigger such a cascade is uncertain. If it did, the debris could endanger replacement satellites for years.
Some radioactive particles could enter the atmosphere and eventually settle on the ground. But a blast in space is too far away to sweep up the soil and water that carry fallout from a surface explosion.
As the particles disperse, their radioactivity decreases over time. The concentrated local fallout that can expose people near a ground-level blast to high doses would be unlikely.

item.title: England logged record 5,258 heat-linked deaths this summer
item.description:
England registered 5,258 deaths linked to this summer’s heat, the highest number of such fatalities on record, the UK’s Health Security Agency (Ukhsa) said in estimates released Tuesday.
“Summer 2026 was an exceptional summer, with the highest mortality observed since 2016, when the Ukhsa began publishing annual heat mortality reports,” the agency said in a provisional report.
Britain experienced its hottest summer on record this year, characterized by early and successive heatwaves.
The country has also seen an exceptional drought that resulted from a lack of rainfall not seen in nearly 200 years.
Scientists say human-driven climate change is amplifying extreme weather events, with Europe warming faster than the global average and heatwaves growing more frequent and severe.
While the provisional figures may be revised, the mortality impact “exceeds that observed in any previous annual heat-associated mortality estimate,” the Ukhsa added.
The latest figure, logged across seven “heat episodes” between May and September, topples the previous record of 2,985 estimated heat-linked deaths in summer 2022.
The Ukhsa analysis compares mortality during periods of heat with mortality during “nearby non-heat periods,” the agency said.
This is particularly useful for understanding the impacts of heatwaves, it added.
Multiple European countries registered record heat-related deaths after a sweltering summer this year, including Germany with 16,300 and more than 5,000 in Spain.
A report published in The Lancet medical journal last month said climate change must be declared a “global health emergency” and found there were more than three million deaths caused by heat between 2016 and 2023.
Heat-related excess deaths often result from the higher risk of heart attacks and strokes caused by the strain of trying to keep body temperatures stable.
Britain’s national weather agency has predicted the El Nino weather pattern could make 2027 the hottest year globally.
Experts are urging the country to better prepare homes and public infrastructure for warmer summers.

item.title: ‘Hopes of 250 million’ for Pakistani on China space mission
item.description:
The first foreign astronaut on a Chinese space mission said on Tuesday that he will be carrying “the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis” when he blasts off from the Gobi Desert on Wednesday.
Beijing has poured billions into the Chinese space program, whose prized Tiangong space station is stewarded by teams of three astronauts, typically rotated every six months.
The Shenzhou-24 mission is set to lift off at 8:18am (0018 GMT) on Wednesday from the Jiuquan launch center in northwest China, China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) spokesman Zhang Jingbo told a news conference on Tuesday.
Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistan Air Force pilot and payload specialist, will be the first foreign astronaut to fly on a Chinese space mission and also the first non-Chinese to board the Tiangong space station.
“I carry the name of Pakistan on my shoulder, the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis,” Ali told a separate news conference held later to introduce the crew.
“To every child who is watching while I’m in orbit, just look up at the sky and remember that I am up there with your dreams,” he said in English, following other remarks in Urdu and fluent Mandarin.
Ali will join a short orbital flight expected to last around five days before returning with the Shenzhou-23 spaceship, which docked at the Tiangong in May.
Pakistani officials welcomed Ali’s selection as a significant step in relations between Islamabad and Beijing, which have blossomed in recent years.
Pakistani Information Minister Attaullah Tarar described the mission as a “source of joy and pride for the entire nation.”
“China and Pakistan are all-weather strategic cooperative partners,” Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing on Tuesday.
Pakistan Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal said the mission underscored the trust and “iron brotherhood” between the two countries.
Ali is not the first Pakistani in space, with Monaco-based polar adventurer Namira Salim having flown on Virgin Galactic’s Galactic 04 mission in October 2023.
China was excluded from the International Space Station (ISS) in 2011 when the United States banned NASA from collaborating with Beijing.
This prompted the Asian giant to invest heavily in its own space activities, landing a probe on the far side of the Moon in 2019 and a rover on Mars in 2021.
China successfully landed a reusable rocket for the first time in July, according to its space agency, marking a major step in its space ambitions and in reducing launch costs.
China is aiming to land astronauts on the Moon before 2030, a race in which the United States is also competing with its Artemis program.
The crew currently aboard the Tiangong space station is headed by 40-year-old Zhu Yangzhu, Lai Ka-ying and Zhang Zhiyuan, also 40.
Lai is Hong Kong’s first astronaut and the only woman currently aboard.
After the new, all-male crew reaches the Tiangong, Pakistan’s Ali will return to Earth alongside Lai and Zhang.
Zhu will remain on board to complete China’s first full-year stay in space -- a key test of endurance critical for future lunar and potentially deep-space ambitions.
Zhu will be accompanied for the next six-month Tiangong rotation by 51-year-old space veteran Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi, in his late thirties and making his first voyage to space.
The Long March-2F rocket that will carry the crew into space will soon be filled with propellant, the CMSA’s Zhang said on Tuesday morning.
The crew is in good condition and the space station is functioning normally, meeting all requirements for the mission, he said.

item.title: Yemen officials say strike on buses, trucks kills 26
item.description:
An airstrike on trucks and buses killed 26 people in Yemen’s southwest, local officials told AFP on Tuesday, as the Houthis and government forces traded blame for the attack.
Yemen, one of the world’s poorest countries, has become the most active front in the Middle East war with the Iran-backed Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition exchanging frequent attacks.
Two officials said coalition warplanes struck Houthi vehicles on Monday in Lahj province, where the group has advanced in recent weeks towards Aden, the government’s interim capital.
The aircraft “targeted two vehicles belonging to the Houthis at the moment when a truck and a bus were passing by, in an area considered a front line,” one of the officials said, adding 12 Houthi fighters and 14 civilians were killed.
The second official confirmed the death toll. Witnesses reported seeing charred bodies at the scene.
The Houthis’ military spokesman blamed the Saudi air force for the strike, saying it would not go “unanswered.”
But government forces said the Houthis carried out the attack.
The pro-Iran group targeted “civilian vehicles bearing no military markings, on a road that is a vital artery for the population”, government forces spokesman Majed al-Nazli said.
Separate strikes on Monday killed 17 people and destroyed several buildings in the coastal province of Hodeida, the Houthis’ telecommunications ministry said.
Yemen, embroiled in more than a decade of civil war, was sucked into the wider US-Iran conflict in July when a truce between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government unraveled.
Since then, the fighting has left more than 1,600 people dead and over 300,000 displaced in the country, the poorest on the Arabian Peninsula, according to the latest UN toll.
The Houthis, who already controlled swathes of Yemen, seized all government positions along the Red Sea coast, tightening their grip on the vital waterway where they have been targeting Saudi oil tankers.
They have also launched near-daily missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, targeting military, civilian and oil infrastructure, while regularly reporting coalition airstrikes on Yemen.
The Houthi attacks have hampered Saudi oil exports and strike at the heart of the kingdom’s efforts to diversify its economy by becoming a tourism, travel and business hub.
The Saudi-led coalition intervened in Yemen in early 2015, after the Houthis had captured the capital Sanaa and sent the internationally recognized government fleeing to Aden.
The war left hundreds of thousands dead and triggered a major humanitarian catastrophe before an uneasy ceasefire went into effect in 2022.

item.title: Jamaat to stage protests outside Dhaka
item.description:
Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami will hold protest rallies and processions in all metropolitan cities outside Dhaka on Wednesday as part of its previously announced program to press for a seven-point set of demands.
Jamaat Secretary General Mia Golam Parwar on Tuesday called on residents of the cities concerned to take part in the program and make it a success.
He said the protests would seek to secure the seven demands of the 11-party alliance and denounce what the party described as sabotage, violence and arson by the ousted Awami League across the country.
Parwar also accused the government of failing to maintain law and order and said the rallies would be held in protest against that failure.
In a statement, he urged people to join the demonstrations spontaneously.

item.title: NCP holds motorcycle rally in Dhaka to resist 'anarchy'
item.description:
National Citizen Party (NCP) on Tuesday organised a motorcycle rally in Dhaka as part of its program to resist what it described as anarchy by the Awami League.
The rally was organised by the NCP's Dhaka North unit and began at 2pm from Manik Mia Avenue.
It passed through Agargaon, Shewrapara, Kazipara and Mirpur-10 before heading towards Mirpur-14 where it was scheduled to end.
NCP Senior Joint Convener and MP Hasnat Abdullah, Senior Joint Member Secretary Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain, Sarjis Alam, Political Council member Ariful Islam and Joint Convener Tarek A Adil, among other central leaders, took part in the rally.
NCP leaders were heard chanting slogans such as “Catch Awami League leaders and put them in jail” and “Don't chant Apa, Apa; your Apa will never return”.

item.description:
A delegation from the International University of Business Agriculture and Technology (IUBAT), led by Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr Abdur Rab, paid a courtesy call on President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir at Bangabhaban on Monday afternoon.
During the meeting, the vice-chancellor briefed the president on the university's academic activities and recent progress.
The president stressed the importance of maintaining quality standards in higher education and urged universities to equip students with the knowledge and skills required for employment and professional life.
The delegation also invited the president, in his capacity as IUBAT's chancellor, to preside over the university's upcoming 10th convocation.
The president accepted the invitation, according to an IUBAT statement.
Secretaries from the President's Office were also present at the meeting.

item.title: Shafiqur leaves Australia for home, cancels Malaysia trip
item.description:
Leader of the Opposition and Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Dr Shafiqur Rahman left Sydney for home on Tuesday after completing a four-day visit to Australia, cancelling his planned one-day trip to Malaysia due to an urgent necessity.
In a post on his verified Facebook post, Shafiqur Rahman said he had been deeply moved by the warmth and hospitality shown by expatriate Bangladeshis during his visit.
He said expatriate Bangladeshis cherished the country, dreamed of its future and wanted to contribute to its development, adding that Bangladesh had a responsibility to give them and all Bangladeshis living abroad the respect they deserved.
The opposition leader said he suspended the planned one-day trip to Malaysia due to an urgent necessity, expressing hope of meeting expatriate Bangladeshis there in the near future.
During the Australia visit, he attended several receptions, discussion sessions and community gatherings involving expatriate Bangladeshis, professionals, academics and community representatives in Sydney and Canberra. Leading a delegation, Shafiqur left Dhaka for Australia on November 20.

item.title: Experts discuss feasibility of solar-powered advanced cold storage technology
item.description:
Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Abdul Awal Mintoo emphasized the expansion of modern solar-powered cold storage technology to reduce post-harvest losses, preserve the quality of fruits and vegetables, and improve farmers’ incomes. He said that linking cold storage facilities with temperature-controlled transportation would enable farmers to bring a greater share of their produce to market, reducing waste and creating new income opportunities.
The Minister made the remarks as chief guest at the closing event of the international research project titled “Feasibility Research of Solar Electric-Based Cold Storage Equipped with Low-temperature Latent Heat Material for Fruits and Vegetables in Bangladesh Climate Conditions,” held on Tuesday, 24 November, at Hotel InterContinental in Dhaka.
He noted that agriculture plays a vital role in Bangladesh’s economy, food security, and rural livelihoods. However, climate change, high temperatures, insufficient cold storage facilities, and irregular electricity supply contribute to substantial post-harvest losses. Addressing these challenges requires the expansion of modern technologies and renewable-energy-based storage solutions.
Referring to a pilot solar-powered cold storage facility installed at an agricultural farm in Rajshahi, the Minister said the technology had been developed with Bangladesh’s climate, agricultural practices, and electricity supply conditions in mind. Lessons from the project could help establish more reliable and environmentally sustainable cold storage facilities in other agricultural regions.
He added that the research findings and pilot experience could inform an integrated cold chain system combining pre-cooling, cold storage, temperature-controlled transportation, and digital temperature monitoring. Such an approach could preserve product quality, strengthen local technical capacity, and support low-carbon agricultural infrastructure.
The international research project was implemented under the leadership of the Korea Institute of Industrial Technology (KITECH), South Korea, in cooperation with Bangladesh’s Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. Financial support was provided by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and the Climate Technology Centre and Network (CTCN). Pacific Solar & Renewable Energy Ltd., Bangladesh, participated as the local industry partner.
The project aimed to evaluate the technical and financial feasibility of a sustainable, energy-efficient, and environmentally friendly cold storage system suited to Bangladesh’s climatic conditions.
The project integrates solar panels with Thermal Energy Storage (TES) and Latent Heat Material (LHM) technology. By storing cooling energy, the system can help maintain stable temperatures inside cold storage chambers when sunlight is unavailable or solar power generation decreases. This creates the potential for an alternative preservation solution in areas with limited electricity supply.
The pilot cold storage system in Rajshahi includes separate pre-cooling and cold storage chambers, solar power generation, thermal energy storage, and temperature-control technology. The project evaluated operational performance, suitability for local weather, technical and financial feasibility, and prospects for scaling up. Technical training for local operation and maintenance was also undertaken.
Speakers at the closing event included Dr. Nurun Nahar, Additional Secretary of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change; Dr. Kim Jong Yeol, Principal Researcher and Project Leader at KITECH; Youngjin Shin, Director of EST Co., Ltd., South Korea; and expert Dr. Inhan Kim. Dr. Mustafa Hasan, Research Director-in-Charge of the Business Research & Consultancy Centre (BRCC), American International University-Bangladesh (AIUB), also attended.
The Minister thanked UNEP, CTCN, KITECH, local industry partners, researchers, experts, and farmers involved in the initiative. He encouraged further innovative, environmentally sustainable, and technology-driven projects in Bangladesh and expressed hope for continued technical cooperation with South Korea and international development partners to expand modern cold storage technology to other agricultural regions.
Representatives of the ministry, Department of Environment, research institutions, local project partners, NGOs, the agriculture and transport sectors, and print and electronic media attended the event.
This Bangladesh–South Korea technology collaboration represents an important step toward renewable energy integration, climate-resilient technologies, and modern cold chain infrastructure in agriculture. Lessons from the project could contribute to reduced post-harvest losses, stronger food security, and more sustainable agricultural infrastructure.
